name: Mahoran Kangué
description: Kangué, meat slow-cooked with only onion and salt and genuinely no added water, is a real, distinctive Mahoran technique - the meat cooks entirely in its own real juices, letting the ingredient's own flavor carry the dish, not a recipe missing steps.
steps_detailed: Combine the beef, onion, and salt in a heavy pot with a tight lid, adding no water at all.
Cover and cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, 45-55 minutes, until the meat is tender and cooked entirely in its own released juices - real kangué depends on this, not on added liquid.

name: Mahoran Rougail
description: Rougail, a tomato-based sauce enriched with real warming spices, genuinely traces back to Réunion Island but has become a common Mahoran accompaniment to meat and fish.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion, garlic, and ginger in a little oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and jalapeño, and simmer 15-18 minutes until thickened.

name: Mahoran Trovi Ya'Nadzi
description: Trovi ya'nadzi, fish and plantain simmered together in real coconut milk, is a beloved Mahoran dish, its real sweet-savory balance being the whole point.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in a little oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the plantain and coconut milk, and simmer 15-18 minutes until the plantain is tender.
Add the fish and simmer 8-10 minutes more until just cooked through.

name: Mahoran Mbawa Ya Tomati
description: Mbawa ya tomati, chicken wings simmered in a real tomato sauce, is a genuine street-food staple shared across Mayotte and Comoros.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion and garlic, 8-9 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 20-22 minutes until the chicken is tender.

name: Mahoran M'tsolola
description: M'tsolola, a hearty stew genuinely combining green banana, cassava, and coconut milk, is shared across Mayotte and the wider Comoros archipelago, real versions built with either fish, beef, or goat.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in a little oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the plantain, cassava, and coconut milk, and simmer 20-22 minutes until nearly tender.
Add the fish and simmer 8-10 minutes more until just cooked through.

name: Mahoran Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Mayotte's rich Indian Ocean and coral reef fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Mahoran Fried Plantain
description: Fried ripe plantain, a common Mahoran side dish, real versions using genuinely ripe plantain for real caramelization.
steps_detailed: Fry the plantain slices in a little oil, turning once, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply caramelized and golden.
